subject: Learning Methods
title: The Cornell Method
description: A fast breakdown of The Cornell Method for builders.

hook.text: Walter Pauk designed the Cornell method at Cornell University in the 1950s.

buildup.text: Divide the page into three sections: a narrow left column for cues, a wide right column for notes, and a summary at.

discovery.text: During class, take notes in the right column. After class, write questions in the left column that the notes answer.

twist.text: The magic is in step two. Writing cue questions forces you to process and transform the material again after class.

climax.text: Cover the right column and quiz yourself using only the cue questions. This turns your notes into a self-testing tool.

punchline.text: Cornell turns notes into quiz cards. Capture and self-test.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the left 'cue' column in Cornell notes?
options: To write the date and topic
To write questions that test the notes in the right column
To record the professor's name and lecture title
